summary: Configured node1 to rotate /var/log/inventory/app.log daily, retain seven gzip-compressed rotations, and preserve open writer continuity with copytruncate. Configuration and data survived the mandatory node reboot.
actions_performed: Created /etc/logrotate.d/inventory with daily, rotate 7, compress, missingok, notifempty, and copytruncate.
Enabled and started the persistent daily logrotate.timer.
Forced a scoped test rotation and verified writes through an already-open descriptor continued afterward.
Safely rebooted node1 and verified its boot identity changed and all required state recovered.

evidence.requirement: Daily rotation with seven compressed archives
evidence.summary: The daily timer is enabled and active; policy parses as a one-day interval with seven retained rotations; an actual gzip archive was created; policy and scheduling remained healthy after reboot.

evidence.requirement: Application can continue writing after rotation
evidence.summary: A writer opened app.log before rotation. Copytruncate retained inode 80283 and the open descriptor; the pre-rotation record moved into app.log.1.gz and the same writer placed the post-rotation record in app.log.

Healthy baseline was captured on boot 4eaf428d-1724-4431-a764-c9e0fdc350cc, the safe reboot was acknowledged, and node1 recovered on boot 26edf1a8-df88-4b2c-b5fa-9a74d4ec47e6 with system state running, timer enabled/active, configuration intact, gzip valid, and current plus archived data preserved.
